questions.stem: What has to match between manifest.json and the files on disk?
options: The lesson title and the first heading in lesson.md
The lesson id and the folder name under lessons/
The course slug and the folder name under courses/
Nothing — the engine discovers lessons by scanning the folder
questions.explanation: The engine fetches lessons/<id>/lesson.md, so the id is the folder name. The course folder name is conventionally the slug but nothing enforces it, and the engine never scans the directory — it only reads what the manifest lists.

questions.stem: Why must a course be served from the repo root rather than from inside the course folder?
options: Because index.html references ../../engine/, which a server rooted in the course folder will not serve
Because localStorage is scoped to the root path
Because marked.js has to be loaded before the manifest
questions.explanation: Simple static servers refuse to serve files above their root. The course shell loads ../../engine/style.css and ../../engine/app.js, so the root has to be the repo. scripts/package-course.sh exists precisely to vendor the engine in when you need a course to stand alone.

questions.stem: A lesson is outlined but not written. What is the correct thing to do?
options: Leave it out of the manifest until it is written
Write a short placeholder paragraph so the course looks complete
Mark it "stub": true with an outline describing what it will cover
Set its quiz pass_threshold_pct to 0 so it can be skipped
questions.explanation: A stub renders its outline, greys out in the sidebar, and is excluded from the progress denominator. Leaving it out of the manifest hides the roadmap from the reader; a placeholder paragraph is filler, which is the specific failure this format is designed to prevent.

questions.stem: You rename a course's slug from "okta-basics" to "identity-basics" after a dozen people have worked through it. What happens?
options: Nothing — progress is keyed on the folder name
Their progress resets, because saved progress is namespaced by slug
The engine migrates their progress automatically
The course fails to load until they clear site data
questions.explanation: Progress is stored under academy-of-things:<slug>:progress in each browser's localStorage. Change the slug and the engine looks up a key that does not exist, so every lesson shows incomplete. Pick a slug you can live with.
